case_name: Smt. Chand Dhawan vs Jawaharlal Dhawan
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1972. In 1985, a petition for divorce by mutual consent was filed. The wife alleged she was not a consenting party and the petition was dismissed. Later, the husband filed a regular petition for divorce alleging adultery against his wife.

legal_principles.principle: An application under section 25 of the Act is not maintainable if no decree has been passed by the Matrimonial Court.
legal_principles.held: The Matrimonial Court at Amritsar, in the earlier litigation, having not passed any decree of the variables known as Restitution of Conjugal Rights, Judicial Separation, Nullity of Marriage, or Divorce, so as to quash proceedings under section 25 and sequently quashing the order under section 24 of the Act.

legal_principles.principle: A court exercising jurisdiction under the Hindu Marriage Act may, at any time subsequent to passing a decree, order maintenance and support for one party.
legal_principles.held: Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing- any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for purpose by either the wife o r the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support.

outcome.final_order: The Court granted her maintenance pendente lite at Rs. 1,000 p.m. and later increased it to Rs. 6,000 as litigation expenses and Rs. 2,000 as maintenance pendente lite.
